title: Cap. V Obj. 2 Sol: will to build precedes coaptation; eternal life given vs destinated
pass_a_gloss: For the first will of building in the mind of the craftsman was not born from foresight of the fitting-together of stones and timbers; but the other way round, from the will of building followed that first joining of stones and timbers. By like reason, eternal life produced in an external effect, and conferred on Peter or Paul, presupposes many things which eternal life as destinated to them in the secret will of God does not prerequire. To destinate to life is an immanent act in the mind of God; to give life or to lead through to life is a work tending outward upon the creature: the former is perfected and completed by the sole act of the Divine will; the latter is not perfected except with many actions of the creature intervening, prerequired by Divine ordination.
pass_b_english: The craftsman's first will to build was not born from foresight of fitting stones and timbers — the reverse: from the will to build followed that first joining of stones and timbers. Likewise eternal life produced outwardly and conferred on Peter or Paul presupposes many things that eternal life as destinated to them in God's secret will does not prerequire. To destinate to life is an immanent act in God's mind; to give life or lead to life is a work tending outward on the creature. The former is finished by the sole act of the divine will; the latter is not finished without many creaturely actions intervening, prerequired by divine ordination.
source_text: Non enim ex praevisa coaptatione lapidum et lignorum nascebatur prima voluntas aedificandi in mente artificis; sed vice versa, ex voluntate aedificandi sequebatur illa prima lapidum et lignorum coagmentatio. Pari ratione, vita aeterna in effectu externo producta, et Petro aut Paulo collata, multa praesupponit quae vita aeterna ut in arcana Dei voluntate illis destinata non praerequirit. Destinare ad vitam, est actus immanens in mente Dei; dare vitam vel perducere ad vitam, est opus ad extra tendens in creaturam: illud perficitur et absolvitur solo actu voluntatis Divinae; hoc non perficitur nisi intervenientibus multis creaturae actionibus ex ordinatione Divina praerequisitis.
